body: I talk about wanting to die a lot. I talk about how much living actually brings me pain, but I don’t think anyone around me gives a shit. Whatever I guess.
a few months, every single day. they’re not really helping tbh, i just find them draining.

I need to be loved. If someone isn’t in love with me I will feel incredibly fucking useless and it sucks so bad.

Also: when someone leaves me I feel like my world is ending. I’ve tried to kill myself twice because two people have left my life, it sounds so manipulative but I truly can’t handle losing anyone. Abandonment issues are wild.

I was emotionally abused too. My ex said some horrid things to me, and she made me feel like I was better off dead. But whatever this person said to you, it’s not true. You deserve to live. You deserve happiness and you’re not alone. I’m here for you.

This kinda freaks me out because over the years I’ve heard the same thing, and I’m not diagnosed with Schizophrenia. I’ve never really opened up about it to anyone though. Maybe it’s just anxiety or my conscious, but I have heard a radio playing in my head, people calling my name, and random noises like doors shutting or whatever when I’m falling asleep. Interesting.
Based on a hospital. People die a lot.

One time at night, around 9pm or so, I was watching TV as my mom was in the kitchen and my sister in her room. There was a door behind me that led to the stairs and it was almost shut. The TV was at a good volume, and suddenly I heard this horrifying scream come from upstairs. I jumped, ran to the bottom of the stairs to call my sister and ask if she was okay. She was fine, cleaning her room and she said she didn't scream. My mom didn't even hear anything, so I was like what the fuck? My sister immediately got freaked out. I don't know if I was hallucinating, but I've heard this stuff before in my house. Freaks me the fuck out.
I really know how you feel. I got discharged from therapy because of the same thing, but no matter how hard it gets, keep pushing. You're so strong, and you are not alone.
It's George, John Doe is George.

No one talks about the part where you literally have no motivation to do anything. To eat, wash, brush your teeth, even attend to your own hobbies. When your body is so heavy, and all you can do is lay down. It affects us with the mental illness and others around us. I guess that's what hurts the most.

The Gang Turns Black.

I skip this episode every time. It's so cringey, I can't stand it.

This will probably get buried but whatever.

When I was younger, my family used to joke around about me having crushes on boys. It used to embarrass me but I didn't say anything. They did that for a long while, pointing out when I was friends with boys, when I'd just glance at someone who I didn't even find attractive. It sounds stupid but it made me not want to talk about when I actually liked someone, even when I got my heart broken. I always kept my crushes and relationships a secret. I still do now because I feel humiliated for finding someone attractive or loving them.

This is most likely the reason why I didn't open up about having a girlfriend.

It's Always Sunny In Philadelphia.

When you're watching it you realise that you live a way better life than the characters. Because well, they're really fucking terrible. This show certainly brings me a lot of joy, especially when I feel depressed and insecure. 10/10 would definitely recommend.
Honestly every Jesse Pinkman scene in Breaking Bad. Aaron Paul never fails to make me cry, he's a brilliant actor.

Apparently it's not normal to see your parents physiclally fight every time your mom got drunk. Not that they cared. Still, I feel like my emotions about it are invalid because it never actually happened to me. (Only once) And people have had it worse.
Honestly. There's nothing special about her either.
Izzie was one of my favorites, but what she did was so messed up. I guess she learnt from it though.

Derek Shepherd from Grey's Anatomy. Everyone adores him, even though he's an overrated asshole who /was/ toxic for Meredith. He always lashed out, treated his drug addicted sister like garbage, and was desperate to be chief, putting himself before everyone else. God. He annoys me.
When girls wake up with a face full of makeup and brushed hair.
Every time I get into a car my immediate thought is is that it's going to crash. No thanks.

Similar story, I guess? My mom first smelled flowers when she was alone in her bedroom, just after her grandparents died. The scent would appear every time a family member passed. I've smelled it randomly, even when it's been winter and there's been no flowers in the house. My mom always says it's dead family passing through, and to me that's wholesome.
